facts.title: Tatev Monastery
facts.text: Above the Vorotan canyon, one of the most renowned centers of learning in the Armenian world.

facts.title: Wings for the builder
facts.text: Tradition recalls the master builder's words at the edge of the abyss: “May God give me wings.”
Saints Peter and Paul, consecrated in 906 in the presence of King Smbat I Bagratuni.

facts.title: The Gavazan
facts.text: An eight-to-nine-meter octagonal pillar, designed to sway without toppling and to warn of seismic tremors.

facts.title: A medieval university
facts.text: Founded by Hovhan Vorotnetsi; his disciple Gregory of Tatev brought its prestige to its zenith.

facts.title: 10,000 manuscripts burned
facts.text: About ten thousand manuscripts were burned in the Seljuk invasions. Then came Tamerlane and Shah Rukh.

facts.title: The “Wings of Tatev”
facts.text: A 5,750-meter aerial tramway above the Vorotan now links Halidzor with the monastery.

ytTitle: Tatev, the monastery perched above the Vorotan Gorge
ytLead: In Syunik, southeastern Armenia, Tatev became the seat of the bishopric in the 9th century and, in the 14th, home to a university: one of the most renowned centers of learning in the Armenian world.
